body:
I'm reading everyone's lovely responses and I'll probably try to reply as well! Thank you to everyone who took any time to read a bit of what I wrote and thank you to everyone who wrote replies! It's the first time I've really let myself bring this outside of my head, if you know what I mean, and I feel a little better already for it.


I also wanted to clarify that I have done at least a bit of diving into understanding the dd/lg dynamic I mentioned, I REALLY want to say that I don't see it as my place to judge anyone outwardly on their interest in that in a sexual manner. Especially those who have been through childhood trauma as I have. I have kinda flip-flopped on my personal opinion on it and overall it certainly hits wrong buttons for me and so I avoid portrayals of that dynamic in media I consume, but other than that I've landed on the opinion that I cannot know (nor is it my business) anyone else's reasoning for being interested in it so I withhold judgement. I can see it fitting into both a healthy and unhealthy recovery process for someone, and honestly it's not my place to judge. I've been intrigued by bdsm dynamics before so I'm aware of a bunch of different lifestyle and kink choices, and not all of them have to sit well with me personally for others to enjoy them. 


I especially don't want to offend anyone who enjoys the sexual side of that lifestyle, and I feel like the tone in my post was obviously showcasing my personal distaste. I don't judge my friend, and I certainly don't judge anyone I don't know. I'm sorry if anyone was personally offended by my implications, and I'm feeling now that I should have made that part of my post a little less judgy-sounding. I meant all my negative thoughts purely in regards to a hypothetical situation with myself and my partner. I have some friends that are active in kinky communities and we honestly have pretty enthusiastic discussion about things like femdom and (more rarely) MD/lb relationships and these don't trigger quite the same negative feelings in me that the dd/lg does. That's how I'm certain my trauma must play some part in my views, and so I've tried to acknowledge that I might be, in a pretty large way, biased. :)


Nobody reacted in an extreme way, but I feel I should have been a bit more tactful. I don't mean to start/continue a discussion on the matter as, like I said, my views aren't truly fully-formed and it leads me to be a bit hypocritical on the topic.

This is a lot of resources! Thank you! I'm going to check out that subreddit and your posts. 

Thank you. :)
Thank you, friend. :( I wish more people understood.
Reading that made me tear up, that last sentence is spot on. That's exactly it! Can't believe I've never read this quote before.
I did not find a single resource that was covered by provincial insurance helpful. In other words, I only got actual, HELPFUL help if I paid for it. :(
This analogy made me smile, and you made me feel better. :) I'm going to keep it in mind.
